_comment: The baked-in default rulebook. docs/03 requires this to become a remote,
Ed25519-signed artifact in Phase 2 — a title-format change at Gmail must be
fixable in six hours, not in a notarisation round. The loader is written so
that swap is a fetch-and-verify step, not a rewrite.
Patterns are written from published window-title formats, deliberately not
from any one person's log. Personalisation is a separate layer: the rulebook
says what a context IS, the Personaliser learns what is unusual FOR YOU.
Seeing any of these opens a grace window and suppresses every rule.
docs/02: fail open — accusing someone of skipping AI right after they used
it is the fastest uninstall available.
Because this suppresses everything, a false positive here is expensive in a
way a missed nudge is not: it silences the product invisibly. So the title
patterns are only consulted for BROWSER windows, where the title is the page
<title>, and they are anchored rather than matched as bare words. A note
called 'Claude', a folder called 'Claude Working Folder', a Slack channel
called #chatgpt — none of those are AI use, and an unanchored word match
treats all three as a ten-minute amnesty.
bundleIds are native AI clients, matched exactly. Only editors that are
AI-native by default belong here; docs/02 accepts the imprecision for those
because in-editor AI use is invisible from outside. A general editor like VS
Code does not qualify — listing it would silence the product for anyone who
writes code all day.
Webmail titles are 'Subject - account@domain - Gmail' or, on Workspace,
'... - <Org> Mail'. Excluding the mailbox-folder titles is what separates
'reading one specific message' from 'staring at an inbox' — the single
highest-value distinction in docs/02, and it needs no page access.
Folder names are localised, so the exclusions carry locale variants.

excludeTitlePatterns: ^(受信トレイ|送信済みメール|下書き)\b

nudge.copy: Still on that one email. Want a draft instead?
nudge.promptTemplate: Here's an email I need to reply to. Draft a concise reply in my voice.

_comment: Triage rather than composition, so lower confidence and a longer fuse.
The unread count lives in the title and changes as you read, so this
matches the folder prefix only — never the whole string.

nudge.copy: Long stretch in the inbox. Want help clearing it?
nudge.promptTemplate: Help me triage and draft replies for a backlog of email.
Help me write a clear response to this conversation thread.

rules._comment: Writing surfaces. A blank-document check needs page access we don't have, so dwell substitutes — see docs/02.

nudge.copy: Blank page winning? Hand it over.
nudge.promptTemplate: Help me outline and draft this document.

nudge.copy: Formula wrangling is a solved problem.
nudge.promptTemplate: Help me with this spreadsheet — formulas, cleanup, or analysis.

rules._comment: Repetition, not dwell: several searches inside one window means the answer isn't being found.

nudge.copy: Third search on this. Just ask properly.
nudge.promptTemplate: I've been searching for this without luck. Answer it properly.

rules._comment: docs/03: the second source quote, built literally. Context-free, so it can never be wrong. Default off, user turns it on.

nudge.copy: Whatever you're doing — want to send it over?
nudge.promptTemplate: Here's what I'm working on. How would you help with it?
